solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Help injured raven found in street

indicators.note: being found in a street means sitting between its letters, so the street abbreviation wraps the rest
an injured bird is knocked out of shape, so the letters of raven are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call for help over a hurt raven discovered lying in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Help' looks like a plea, but it is a noun for a domestic worker; 'injured' gives ERVAN and 'found in' puts it in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A help is an old-fashioned word for a domestic employee, someone paid to do household work.

clue.text: Pitt oddly neglected to stop fraud when in office

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to fill it, so the pick plugs a gap in the word for fraud

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick

indicators.note: neglecting the odd letters leaves only the even ones of Pitt

explanation.surface: Pitt the Younger, while prime minister, ignored fraud for odd reasons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly neglected' keeps the even letters; 'to stop' means plug, as with a stopper, not halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting member or tenant is the current holder of the position.

clue.text: Hint of desperation in Orient's poor performance

indicators.note: poor means shabbily put together, so the letters are reworked
a hint gives just the first letter, here of desperation

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: Leyton Orient, a London football club, put in a desperate, poor display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges D, IN and ORIENT; 'in' looks like a link but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a performance or interpretation of a song, piece or role.

clue.text: A passage from Isaiah fills man with hope at last

indicators.note: filling means occupying the inside, so the book's abbreviation goes within the other letters

parts.note: Al is a man's name
Is is the standard abbreviation for the Book of Isaiah

indicators.note: at last points to the last letter of hope

explanation.surface: A Bible reading from Isaiah gives a man fresh hope at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A passage from Isaiah' reads as a Bible verse, but 'A passage' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or theatre.

clue.text: What Astaire was originally doing around North Carolina is featured in record by Queen

indicators.note: being featured in something means appearing inside it, so the pieces go within the record

parts.note: a tape is a recording

indicators.note: originally points to the first letters of doing and around

parts.note: NC is the US abbreviation for North Carolina
R is short for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: Fred Astaire's early career in North Carolina appears on a record with the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: DANC goes inside TAPE, then R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was the famous film dancer who performed in metal-tipped shoes.

clue.text: Excuse of sailor on crack

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the standard crossword sailor
to crack a puzzle or code is to work it out

explanation.surface: A seaman offers his excuse while high on crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' reads as the drug, but it is the verb meaning to work something out.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse a wrongdoer is to forgive or pardon them, releasing them from blame.

clue.text: Regarding a spell

parts.note: a bout is a spell or period of activity

explanation.surface: Concerning a magic spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like magic, but it is a period of time, a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: About and regarding are synonymous prepositions meaning concerning.

clue.text: A material witness's back, hip and knees get broken

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, of witness here
broken things are smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crucial witness in court suffers broken limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A material witness' looks like a legal term, but 'A material' is the definition; S, HIP and KNEES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepskin is a hide with fleece attached, a material used for coats and rugs.

clue.text: Sincere about touring Thailand in the near future

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the letters wrap around the abbreviation
about means turned around, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: real means genuine or sincere
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: Genuinely intending to visit Thailand soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses REAL to LAER, which goes around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a future time, soon after now.

clue.text: Stuff lining space shuttle's tail in transit

indicators.note: lining means placed along the inside, so the word for stuff sits between the other pieces

parts.note: an en is a printer's space

indicators.note: a tail is the end, the last letter of shuttle

parts.note: to stuff an opponent is to rout them

explanation.surface: Material lines the rear of a space shuttle on its journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space' is the printer's unit, not outer space; 'lining' puts the defeat word between the space and the tail letter.
explanation.definitionFit: En route, French for on the way, means while travelling.

clue.text: Ministers to have an influence on society

parts.note: to tend is to conduce or have an influence towards some result

explanation.surface: Church ministers ought to exert some influence on the wider community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ministers' looks like a plural noun for clergy, but with 'to' it is a verb meaning looks after.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean caring for someone's needs, as a nurse looks after the sick.

clue.text: Kettle element

parts.note: kettling is the police tactic of penning demonstrators in a cordon, so one element of a kettle is a person demonstrating

explanation.surface: A heating part inside an electric kettle.
explanation.walkthrough: The heating element of a kettle is the obvious reading; kettling is a British police crowd-control tactic of confining marchers in a small area.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonstrators held in a police cordon make up the kettle, so each is one of its elements.

clue.text: Travelling with Italian nurses can lead to naughtiness after a time

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold closely, so the Italian abbreviation holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: IT is a common abbreviation for Italian (as in Italian vermouth)

indicators.note: after places the pick from naughtiness behind the period of time

parts.note: a can is a tin
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: the lead to a word is its first letter, here of naughtiness

explanation.surface: Going on the road with Italian nurses can lead to mischief before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like a plural noun but is the containment verb; 'after' sets N behind ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant describes someone who travels from place to place, such as a wandering preacher or worker.

clue.text: Hidden in country houses close to Bedford

indicators.note: a country that houses something has it inside, so the letter goes within the country's name

parts.note: Peru is a South American country

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here of Bedford

explanation.surface: Something concealed in rural homes near the town of Bedford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country houses' reads as stately homes, but it is a country containing a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdu, borrowed from French, means lost to view or lying concealed, as a soldier lying in ambush.

clue.text: Restaurant owner eventually having a breather? Just the opposite

indicators.note: having means containing, so one piece holds another
the reverse of the stated arrangement, so the breather holds the letter rather than the letter holding the breather

parts.note: a gill is the breathing organ of a fish

indicators.note: eventually points to what comes at the end, the last letter of owner

explanation.surface: A restaurateur finally gets a break, or rather it gets him.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, R would contain GILL; 'Just the opposite' flips this so GILL contains R.
explanation.definitionFit: A grill, or grillroom, is an eating house specialising in grilled food.

clue.text: Study during course to become a licensed preacher

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a course of bricks is a layer
to read is to study, as reading law

explanation.surface: Studying in a course to qualify as a preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like a course of study, but it is a layer of bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay reader is a layperson authorised by a bishop to conduct some services.

clue.text: Girl stifling an expression of surprise at Mark's defeat

indicators.note: stifling smothers something within, so the girl's name wraps the other pieces

parts.note: Cate is a girl's name, as in Cate Blanchett
heck is a mild exclamation of surprise
M is an abbreviation for mark, once the German currency

explanation.surface: A young woman suppresses a gasp at someone called Mark being beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark's' looks like a man's name, but it supplies M, the abbreviation for mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate in chess ends the game with the king trapped; figuratively it means total defeat.

clue.text: See about unravelling tangle in a simple and effective way

definitions.text: in a simple and effective way

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cathedral city's letters go around the rearranged ones

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, Ely being one in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: unravelling a knot sorts out its strands, so the letters of tangle are rearranged

explanation.surface: Look at how to sort out a tangle neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like look, but it is a bishop's diocese; 'unravelling' gives LEGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant can describe a solution that is neat and ingenious, as in an elegant proof.

clue.text: Former president returning to instil leaderless people with vigour

indicators.note: to instil is to put in, so the reversed name goes inside the shortened word
leaderless means losing the first letter

parts.note: a nation is a people

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the name reads backwards

parts.note: Idi Amin was president of Uganda

explanation.surface: A former leader returns to give energy to a people lacking guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: Idi Amin was Uganda's dictator-president; 'returning' gives NIMA and 'leaderless' gives ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness or spirit.

clue.text: Imagine Frank having no commitments

parts.note: to fancy something is to imagine it
franked mail travels free of charge, so frank means free

explanation.surface: Picture a man named Frank who is unattached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name, but it is the old sense of free of charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy-free describes someone unattached and unconstrained, particularly not in love.

clue.text: Fool of a lawyer turned on dad right away

indicators.note: on puts the reversed lawyer after, in a down clue
right away means the letter for right is taken away

parts.note: a dad is a father

indicators.note: turned means turned around, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: An idiot of a lawyer suddenly turned against his father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like immediately, but it removes R; 'turned' gives AD, and DA is an American district attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Fathead is an informal word for a stupid person.

clue.text: Jack in conversation maintain Peto's ingenuous

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the spoken word holds the setter's letter within
in conversation means as spoken, with the silent K lost

parts.note: the jack in a pack of cards is also called the knave
the setter Peto refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: Jack, chatting, insists that the setter Peto is innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conversation' gives the spoken form NAVE, and 'maintain' sets I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive and ingenuous are synonyms, both meaning innocent and unsuspecting.

clue.text: Extremely happy when high

definitions.meaning: lofty, of high rank or position

explanation.surface: Very happy when on a high.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: overjoyed, and elevated in rank, as an exalted position.

clue.text: Wrong to take last piece of chocolate cake

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: the last piece of a word is its final letter, of chocolate here

explanation.surface: It's wrong to take the final slice of chocolate gateau.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered cake of Central European origin, as Sachertorte.

clue.text: Sally's going over earliest of pamphlets by Swift

indicators.note: going over something covers it, so the raid wraps the letter

parts.note: a sally is a sudden military sortie, a raid

indicators.note: the earliest letter of pamphlets

explanation.surface: Sally is reviewing the first of Jonathan Swift's pamphlets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like Jonathan Swift, the satirist, but means fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift are synonyms, both meaning very fast.

clue.text: Maria not failing to stand by absent lover

indicators.note: to stand by means to sit next to, so the abbreviation is placed beside the rearranged letters
failing means breaking down, so the letters of Maria not are rearranged

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for absent, as in a register

explanation.surface: Maria remains loyal to her lover who is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges MARIA NOT to INAMORAT, and 'to stand by' puts A beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, a sweetheart or mistress, from Italian.

clue.text: Foolish of writer to flip through it

indicators.note: going through something means passing inside it
flipping something turns it over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writer

explanation.surface: It is silly for an author to flick through a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flip through' reads as browsing; 'to flip' gives NEP and 'through' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking skill, and can also mean foolish or out of place.

clue.text: It's seen in Tacoma, Harrisburg and somewhere in Nebraska

indicators.note: seen in means visible within the words, across Tacoma and Harrisburg

explanation.surface: A US place name seen in Tacoma and Harrisburg, and another in Nebraska.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in the US state of Nebraska.

clue.text: Appropriate old books containing exercises to cut out

indicators.note: the first pieces hold the others between them

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books
PE is physical education, school exercises
to die is to stamp out a shape with a die

explanation.surface: Fitting to drop exercises from old textbooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out' looks like delete but is the die-stamping sense, and 'containing' splits the outer pair around the inner pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means suitable or advantageous in the circumstances, perhaps more practical than principled.

clue.text: Some idealistic celebrities make it up

indicators.note: some means a portion of the word idealistic, letters lying within it

explanation.surface: Some idealistic stars invent things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make it up' looks like lying, but means compose; the definition is the group the stars form.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the top tier of famous people, so celebrities compose it.

clue.text: Rushed back to meet accomplished philosopher

indicators.note: to meet means joining up with, so the two pieces sit side by side, the accomplished one first

parts.note: to have accomplished a task is to have done it

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: tore means rushed, as in tore down the road

explanation.surface: Hurried back to meet a gifted thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives EROT; 'accomplished' looks like gifted but means done.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot was an eighteenth-century French Enlightenment thinker, editor of the Encyclopédie.

clue.text: Longed for Dicky, Rex and Dean to follow you at one time

indicators.note: to follow puts the rearranged letters after the archaic pronoun

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of you

indicators.note: dicky means unsound or shaky, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: R stands for Rex, king

explanation.surface: Dicky, Rex and Dean all once wished to follow you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name in a list but is the anagram signal for R and DEAN, giving ARNED.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for or desire something intensely.
